title: The land
evidence: Summary written from the cited sources
text: In March 2010 the Greater Noida Authority allotted a 204,000 sq m group-housing plot, GH-08 in Sector-1, to a consortium led by Supertech with Panchsheel Buildtech as a member. A 30,000 sq m sub-plot, GH-08A, was leased to Panchsheel the same year. Within a year, court rulings on land acquisition in Greater Noida West halted building across the area until 2012.

title: Building twelve towers
evidence: Summary written from the cited sources
text: A revised plan approved in May 2014 kept seven towers of stilt + 14 floors (T1-T7) and added five taller ones: T8-T9 at stilt + 24, T10-T11 at stilt + 20 and T12 at stilt + 21, for 1,312 homes. The later towers were registered with UP RERA in three phases. Tower-10 received its completion certificate in October 2018; by 2019 ten towers were occupied, and the last phase was recorded complete in January 2021.

title: Residents organise
evidence: Summary written from the cited sources
text: Residents registered an apartment owners' association, reported in February 2023 with a nine-member board under registration GBN/10037/2022-2023. In March 2024 an election under an administration-appointed officer chose a new board, which said its first goal was taking over the society from the builder.

title: Handover and everyday services
evidence: Summary written from the cited sources
text: Through 2024 the AOA held meetings on handover, an MOU with the builder and NPCL multipoint electricity. In May the Authority directed the builder to hand over maintenance and the electricity connection by 15 July; in July the MOU was still "in progress". The AOA took over maintenance on 7 September 2024, by its own records, but the electricity connection stayed in the builder's name. The same year saw water shortages, power-cut protests and complaints about lifts, the pool and maintenance charges, with the AOA, the MP and authorities approached.

title: Elections in dispute
evidence: Summary written from the cited sources
text: The board elected in March 2025 was challenged. Deputy Registrar orders, SDM decisions and two High Court judgments followed, with the courts sending questions back to the administrators. In September 2026 the SDM reportedly upheld the 2025 election; a new petition was registered in the High Court in November 2026 and was pending.

title: Where things stand
evidence: Summary written from the cited sources
text: Open questions in late 2026 include the AOA election process; NPCL's mandatory multipoint conversion, which its October notice says about 200 residents opposed; registry for Tower-11 and 12 owners, where the Authority gave the builder until about October 2026 to obtain completion and execute sub-leases; a tax-tribunal order on passing benefits to Tower-10 buyers; and resident demands for public accounts. Each is tracked here with what the public record shows and what it does not.
